newsitem.title: USA: Dow ends lower but tech rebound boosts Nasdaq.
newsitem.headline: Dow ends lower but tech rebound boosts Nasdaq.

text.p: Signs of moderating economic growth briefly rallied bonds and stocks, but gains in U.S. blue chips faded as investors again weighed the slowing economy's impact on corporate profits.
"A slowing economy is a double-edged sword. On the one side rates may ease, but on the other side the slowdown may mean slower earnings momentum," said Marty Kearney, a trader at PTI Securities.
The Dow lost 14 to about 5993. After shedding 25 points the past four sessions, the Nasdaq Composite rose three to 1206.
Stronger technology shares included IBM, up 7/8 to 126-3/8, Intel, up 2-1/2 to 106-3/4, 3Com, up 3-1/2 to 66, and Microsoft, up 7/8 to 136-1/4.

"Techs are doing a bit better. But by and large it was an uneventful day. We had good economic numbers (GDP for Q3) and bonds rallied and then fell when home sales were not as down as expected," said Hildegard Zagorski, Prudential Securities market analyst. She said investors were awaiting Friday's October jobs report "and hanging out to see what happens to the election (next Tuesday). A Democratic Congress won't sit well (with) the markets."
The long bond, which jumped two points Tuesday on bond-friendly third-quarter Employment Cost Index and October consumer confidence reports, lost 7/32 to yield 6.70 percent.
Losers and gainers were about even on heavy NYSE volume of about 439 million shares.

"We're in a pause to refresh," said Alfred Goldman, technical research director at A.G. Edwards. "We're in a normal correctional phase, Day 8. We've come 1,000 (Dow) points since mid-July. The Dow is up 18 percent, Nasdaq is up 28 percent." He added, "It's still a bull market. Why not a correction when the election is six days off?"

As for economic news, the Commerce Department said the economy grew at a 2.2 percent pace in the third quarter. That exceeded Gross Domestic Product forecasts of a 1.8 percent annual rate but was far slower than the second quarter's 4.7 percent pace and confirmed a decelerating economic trend.
Bonds later fell on news that September U.S. new home sales fell 0.5 percent to an annualized rate of 816,000 units. The forecast had been for a 768,000 reading.
The Federal Reserve's Beige Book said pressure for wage increases is rising across the country despite a somewhat slower pace of economic growth.

Retailers fell amid signs that consumer spending was slowing. Goldman Sachs downgraded the sector. Wal-Mart lost one to 26-3/8, Gymboree fell 2-1/4 to 31, TJX was off 2-1/4 to 39, and Dillard shed 7/8 to 30-7/8. Dow components Sears and Woolworth were off 1-1/2 to 47, and 1/2 to 21, respectively.

Among other stocks, CompUSA came under a second day of brisk selling, off 5-3/4 to 45-3/4 after confirming some investor fears that retail sales were "somewhat sluggish." CompUSA shed 5-7/8 on Tuesday after Salomon Brothers noted an industrywide softening of retail computer sales.
Elsag Bailey slumped 5-3/4 to 16-7/8 in U.S. trading.

The Netherlands-based maker of equipment and systems for industrial process control reported in-line quarterly results, but warned of soft markets and orders. Merrill, Alex. Brown, Salomon and McDonald & Co downgraded the stock.
Dominick's Supermarket, the second largest supermarket operator in the greater Chicago metropolitan area, rose 1-3/8 to 19-3/8 in its Wall Street debut.

Bay Networks rose 2-1/4 to 20-5/8 after naming a top Intel official, David House, as chairman and chief executive, a move industry analysts said could give Bay the strong hand it lacked. Paul Severino is the current chairman and acting CEO.

Vons Cos rallied 11-1/4 to 54-3/8 after supermarket chain Safeway Inc offered to acquire it in a stock deal that values Vons at $3.25 billion. Safeway, which now has a 34.5 percent stake in Vons outstanding stock, lost 1-3/8 to 42. Vons said it will study the offer.
Carter Wallace surged 3-1/4 to 15 after news it received a letter from Davis Cos saying it was prepared to negotiate the acquisition of all outstanding Carter stock at $18 a share.
Imation climbed 4-7/8 to 27-5/8 after reporting a profit in its first quarter as an independent company. It was spun off from Minnesota Mining & Manufacturing.
Nuco2 slumped 6-1/2 to 12-1/2. Raymond James downgraded the stock.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 3.18 to 1206.23.
The S&P 500 index fell 0.60 to 700.90.
(Figures official as of 1645 EST/2145 GMT)
-- Wall Street desk 212 859 1721
